A function component can be a function declaration, a function expression, or an arrow function. A codebase that mixes all three is harder to scan and search.

By default a named component must be a function declaration, and an unnamed one must be a function expression.

`--fix` rewrites the component in the expected style where it can.

## Configure

Off by default. To turn it on:

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"react/function-component-definition" = "error" # or "warn"
```

Every option, set to its default:

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"react/function-component-definition" = ["error", {
  namedComponents = "function-declaration",
  unnamedComponents = "function-expression",
}]
```

## Examples

Reported:

```jsx
const Greeting = props => {
  return <h1>Hello, {props.name}</h1>;
};

const Footer = function (props) {
  return <footer>{props.text}</footer>;
};
```

Not reported:

```jsx
function Greeting(props) {
  return <h1>Hello, {props.name}</h1>;
}

function Footer(props) {
  return <footer>{props.text}</footer>;
}
```

## Options

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `namedComponents` | `"function-declaration"` | The style for a component that's a function declaration or a function assigned to a variable: `"function-declaration"`, `"function-expression"`, or `"arrow-function"`. |
| `unnamedComponents` | `"function-expression"` | The style for any other component, such as one returned from a function: `"function-expression"` or `"arrow-function"`. |

Each option also takes a list of styles. Every style in the list is allowed, and `--fix` rewrites to the first one.

```jsx
function Greeting(props) {
  return <h1>Hello, {props.name}</h1>;
}
```

```jsx
const Greeting = props => {
  return <h1>Hello, {props.name}</h1>;
};
```

```jsx
function Greeting(props) {
  return <h1>Hello, {props.name}</h1>;
}

const Footer = props => {
  return <footer>{props.text}</footer>;
};
```

An unnamed component:

```jsx
function withTheme(theme) {
  return function (props) {
    return <div className={theme}>{props.children}</div>;
  };
}
```

```jsx
function withTheme(theme) {
  return props => {
    return <div className={theme}>{props.children}</div>;
  };
}
```
